findings.issue: SPEC-02 requires every sub-check to be proven by a corrupted state, but several spec-listed clauses within C1, C3, P1, P5, K2 and L5 have no case. Removing any of them leaves the whole suite green, so a broken implementation of these clauses would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Mutation run on a scratch copy (invariants.test.ts + invariants.acceptance.test.ts + runner.test.ts). Each of these mutants SURVIVED: (1) C1 drop `streetContribution > totalContribution`; (2) C3 drop `|| !balanced` (per-award winner shares sum to award.amount); (3) K2 drop `players.some(p => p.holeCards.length !== 2)`; (4) P1 drop `playerAt(state, seat) !== undefined` (seat not dealt in), and without it P3's `as PlayerState` cast throws on a pot holding chips, which breaks 'never throws'; (5) P5 drop `|| p.totalContribution <= 0`; (6) L5 drop `last.street !== before.street`; (7) L5 drop `after.length !== before.actions.length + 1`. A C4 mutant was killed, which confirms the harness works.
findings.fix: Add one stateCases/stepCases row per clause: C1 `withPlayers(S,{5:{streetContribution:5}})` (street > total); C3 a two-award foldOut result whose totals match but whose shares are moved between awards; K2 `withPlayers(S,{3:{holeCards:[10]}})`; P1 `withPot(S,16,[2,3,4,5,7])`; P5 a winner with totalContribution 0 who is listed as eligible; L5 a result whose last record has street 'preflop', and one with an extra duplicated record. Assert the exact message for each.

findings.issue: The raise half of L4 (`amount !== before.currentBet + unit`) can never fire after L3 passes. legalActions computes raiseTo with the same formula (`hand.ts:226`), so any raise in the legal set already matches. No test covers it, and the mutant that removes it survives. Only the bet half is exercised, through the artificial `currentBet: -1` before-state, which pushes legalActions into its bet branch. That test is valid but checks a state the engine can't produce.
findings.evidence: Mutation L4raise SURVIVED. Coverage reports the line-84 branch as partly uncovered. legalActions: `const raiseTo = state.currentBet + unit`.
findings.fix: Keep it as the A-4 guard, but add a comment saying it only guards against a future legalActions change. Alternatively, test it through a step whose `before.stakes` differs from the stakes legalActions used, which isn't possible. If neither is acceptable, record it as accepted untested defensive code.

findings.issue: A wrong hole-card count is reported with the board/burn template, e.g. `flop has 3 board and 1 burn cards`. Those numbers are correct for the flop, so the message hides the real fault (a seat holding 1 or 3 cards). The spec's single K2 template forces this.
findings.evidence: cardsMessage folds `players.some(p => p.holeCards.length !== 2)` into the same `if` as the board/burn length check and returns the street template.
findings.fix: Propose a spec amendment (the D-2 template was user-approved) to add `seat <s> has <n> hole cards`, and return that message from the hole-card clause. Until then, leave it.

findings.issue: When award totals match contributions but one award's winner shares don't sum to its amount, and the shares still total the same overall, the message reads `awards pay $20 but players put in $20`, which names no fault.
findings.evidence: `awarded !== total ? awarded : paid`. With paid === total and only `balanced` false, both numbers are equal.
findings.fix: For the per-award case, report the award itself, e.g. `<pot> awards $<amount> but winners get $<shares>`. This needs a template amendment. Otherwise put the pot name in the existing wording.

findings.issue: `if (hand === null || hand.violation === null) return ''` guards a state that summarize can't produce: violations > 0 implies a hand with a non-null violation. It is also the only uncovered line range in cli.ts (135-143 branch).
findings.evidence: Coverage: cli.ts uncovered branch 135-143. summarize sets firstViolation whenever any hand.violation !== null.
findings.fix: Keep it only if the type narrowing needs it. Otherwise narrow with a non-null assertion, or pass firstViolation from formatReport's condition (`summary.firstViolation?.violation`).

findings.issue: actionText repeats describeAction's wording for the five player action types. The spec allowed delegating (optional), so the two copies can now drift apart.
findings.evidence: cli.ts:156-167 and invariants.ts:38-51 contain the same strings.
findings.fix: Optional: in actionText, handle only the two blind types and delegate the rest to describeAction(toAction(record)).

summary: The implementation matches the spec. Each invariant is computed independently of the engine: chips use their own arithmetic, bet-cap recounts the action history alongside betCount, pot-eligibility and cards use their own tables and bitmap, and L4/L5 re-derive the betting unit and history. L3 relies on the engine's legalActions, as A-4 accepts. Each of the five faults affects exactly one invariant, and AC#2 asserts that every other id stays 0. A false-positive sweep of 640,000 clean hands (sizes 3-10, four seeds, 20k hands each) found 0 violations. A raise-every-time policy produced only bet-cap violations. workflow.test.ts gained only additions: the playtest command in the ordered list and a new SPEC-08 test, with nothing removed or weakened. The D-6 replacement in runner.test.ts keeps every original assertion for the rejected case and tightens the over-cap case (violations >= 1 became exactly 3). The 1,322 vs 1,150 line overrun comes mostly from formatter wrapping, JSDoc on the new interfaces and the full-string SPEC-07 expectation. I found no avoidable bloat worth cutting. One MAJOR: the SPEC-02 unit tests prove only one clause of several multi-clause sub-checks, and 7 targeted mutants survive. The other findings are MINOR or NIT.
